title: Cap. IX Arg. 4 Sol: infants of unbelieving idolaters — rejection without foresight of the reprobate's unbelief; Vasquez also grants some adult reprobation before foresight of sins
pass_a_gloss: But unto certain infants (for example those taken up from both parents an unbelieving idolater, not knowing Christ, worshipping the devil — whom the Apostle himself marked as unclean, 1 Cor. vii. 14.) sufficient media were not prepared or administered: In such therefore they are compelled to acknowledge rejection without respect unto the foresighted and preconsidered unbelief of the reprobated person. But setting aside infants who, Divine providence so ordaining, are born and die outside the Church, the same Vasquez also grants this, that even as to adults possessed of reason and free will, some reprobation and repulse was predetermined by God from before the foresight of sins, ibid. cap. 2. But by reprobation he understands rejection from that special grace which, being denied, a man always hardens and rushes into perdition, cap. 5.
pass_b_english: Take infants born of two unbelieving idolatrous parents — knowing no Christ, serving the devil — whom the Apostle himself calls unclean (1 Cor. 7:14): for them sufficient media were neither prepared nor administered. In such cases they must grant rejection with no regard to foresight of the reprobate's unbelief. Set those infants aside who, under divine providence, are born and die outside the Church: the same Vasquez also grants that even for adults with reason and free will some reprobation and repulse was fixed by God before foresight of sins (ibid. cap. 2). By reprobation he means rejection from that special grace which, denied, leaves a man always hardening and rushing into perdition (cap. 5).
source_text: Sed quibusdam infantibus (puta ex utroque parente infideli idololatra, Christum nesciente, diabolum colente, susceptis, quos ἀκάθαρτοι ipse Apostolus indigitavit, 1 Cor. vii. 14.) sufficientia media non fuere praeparata aut administrata: In talibus ergo coguntur agnoscere rejectionem absque respectu ad praevisam et praeconsideratam personae reprobatae infidelitatem. Sed missis infantibus, qui Divina providentia ita ordinante nascuntur et moriuntur extra Ecclesiam, Idem Vasques et illud largitur, Et a praevisione peccatorum, etiam quoad adultos et rationis ac liberi arbitrii compotes, fuisse aliquam reprobationem et repulsam a Deo praefinitam, ibid. cap. 2. Reprobationem autem intelligit, rejectionem ab illa gratia speciali, qua negata homo semper indurescit et in perditionem ruit, cap. 5.
